properties.name: Sahel Zone
properties.principle: Climate: the semi-arid belt between the Sahara and the Sudanian savanna, from the Atlantic to the foot of the Eritrean highlands, where mean annual rainfall lies between 100 and 700 mm (CHIRPS v2.0, 1981-2024 mean): the Saharan-Sahelian and Sahelian climates of Wikipedia's 'Sahel', the source Starcom's zone:sahel cites. OECD/SWAC's narrower 200-600 mm Sahel is measured inside each Sector. The isohyets are smoothed over about 60 km and move from year to year; the eastern limit (the escarpment's foot) and the lines between Sectors are drawn here along escarpments, valleys and wetlands, not borders. Liptako-Gourma alone is an operational region (the three-border area), still drawn along physical lines.

properties.name: Atlantic Sahel
properties.character: The Sahel's Atlantic end: the Senegal River valley and its floodplain, the Ferlo and the Mauritanian south up to the Affole hills, where flood-recession farming and irrigated rice meet transhumance and the river is the border. CHIRPS 1981-2024 mean rainfall: median 333 mm (10% of it below 142, 10% above 610); 67% lies in OECD/SWAC's 200-600 mm core.

properties.name: Hodh and Inner Niger Delta
properties.character: The Hodh's pastoral basin and the Inner Niger Delta, the Sahel's great floodplain, with the Mema and the lakes below Timbuktu: rice, fish and the herds' dry-season pasture, and the heart of central Mali's conflict. CHIRPS 1981-2024 mean rainfall: median 292 mm (10% of it below 132, 10% above 589); 63% lies in OECD/SWAC's 200-600 mm core.

properties.name: Liptako-Gourma
properties.character: The three-border area of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger: the Gourma inside the Niger's bend, the Seno plain, the Liptako and the Tillaberi plains, the operational region where the Sahel's armed groups contest the most ground. CHIRPS 1981-2024 mean rainfall: median 276 mm (10% of it below 111, 10% above 600); 55% lies in OECD/SWAC's 200-600 mm core.

properties.name: Niger–Nigeria Sahel
properties.character: The Hausa plains on both sides of the Niger-Nigeria line, from the Dallol Bosso to the Hadejia-Nguru wetlands, with Agadez at the Air's foot: millet and groundnut country, trade and migration routes north, and the banditry of Nigeria's north-west. CHIRPS 1981-2024 mean rainfall: median 267 mm (10% of it below 115, 10% above 582); 53% lies in OECD/SWAC's 200-600 mm core.

properties.name: Lake Chad Basin
properties.character: The lands round Lake Chad: the lake's islands and swamps, Kanem's dunes, Borno and Diffa on the Komadugu Yobe, and the Chari-Logone confluence at N'Djamena, where four countries meet and the jihadist insurgency began. CHIRPS 1981-2024 mean rainfall: median 300 mm (10% of it below 141, 10% above 619); 66% lies in OECD/SWAC's 200-600 mm core.

properties.name: Batha and Lake Fitri
properties.character: Central Chad's plains between the Bahr el Ghazal and the Ouaddai uplands, drained by the Batha into Lake Fitri: herders' country on the transhumance corridors between the Sahara's edge and the Guera hills. CHIRPS 1981-2024 mean rainfall: median 365 mm (10% of it below 146, 10% above 626); 66% lies in OECD/SWAC's 200-600 mm core.

properties.name: Ouaddaï and Darfur
properties.character: The upland block from the Ouaddai massif to the Darfur plateau and Jebel Marra, astride the Chad-Sudan line: one theatre of war, refugee camps and cross-border supply since 2003 and again since 2023. CHIRPS 1981-2024 mean rainfall: median 365 mm (10% of it below 133, 10% above 643); 54% lies in OECD/SWAC's 200-600 mm core.

properties.name: Nile, Butana and Barka
properties.character: The Sahel's eastern end: the White and Blue Niles and their confluence at Khartoum, the Gezira scheme, the Butana plain, the Gedaref and Kassala clay plains and Eritrea's Barka and Gash lowlands up to the foot of the highlands. CHIRPS 1981-2024 mean rainfall: median 297 mm (10% of it below 127, 10% above 615); 56% lies in OECD/SWAC's 200-600 mm core.
